newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips rise as data suggest strong profits.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips rise as data suggest strong profits.

text.p: Stocks rose Monday as a series of upbeat economic reports brightened earnings prospects for U.S. corporations.
"The news was not good for bonds but the worry for the stock market lately has been about companies' 1997 earnings," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
"The hint today is that you can worry a little less because business activity is strong enough."

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 31.44 points to 5,904.36. In the broader market, advancing issues beat decliners 12-9 on volume of 199 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 1.05 to 1,231.10. The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks climbed 3.22 points to 689.41.
The Commerce Department said new single-family home sales rose a surprisingly strong 4.7 percent in August to an annual rate of 832,000 units, the highest rate in more than 10 years.

Economists had expected a decline instead and the robust report sent the inflation-wary bond market sliding. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond, which prior to the report had posted solid gains, fell 10/32 to yield 6.93 percent, up from 6.91 percent at Friday's close.
The news boosted shares in cyclical businesses, such as autos and retailing.

Chrysler Corp., which reached a tentative labour agreement with the United Auto Workers on Sunday, gained 3/4 to 28-7/8. Ford Motor Co. and General Motors Corp. were also higher, with Ford up 3/4 at 31-3/8 and GM up 5/8 at 47-7/8.
J.C. Penney Co. Inc. rose 1-5/8 to 54-3/4 and the NYSE's most active issue, Kmart Corp., gained 1 to 10-1/4 after Morgan Stanley upgraded the company to strong buy.
Other data released Monday showed U.S. personal income and consumer spending each rose 0.6 percent in August, in line with economists' forecasts.

The Chicago Purchasing Managers index registered a reading of 56.3 from 60.0 in August, slightly ahead of forecasts. An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 suggests expansion.
While stocks mustered a rally on the reports, analysts were already looking ahead to figures due later this week as holding the key for the market's near-term performance.
"The big numbers continue to be the unemployment and consumer and producer price numbers," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Monthly unemployment, payrolls and wage data are all due Friday. Consumer and producer price reports are due next week.

Among individual issues, Micro Warehouse Inc. fell 8-7/8 to 22-5/8 after the company said it would likely restate its 1994 and 1995 results after finding errors in its accounting procedures. The company said it believed the action would result in an after-tax charge of about $18 million.

ADT Ltd. fell 7/8 to 19 after the company announced the termination of its merger agreement with Republic Industries Inc. Shares in Republic Industries, which had fallen since announcing in July it would acquire ADT for stock, jumped 1-5/8 to 28-7/8.
